17.t: Working with data: finding a fault
q: State the voltage across L1 with the switch closed.
Explain why the switch reads 6.0 V when it is open.
The open switch is the gap: the whole battery voltage is across it and no current flows.
L2 does not light. Use the data to suggest two possible faults.
L2 has 0 V across it, so it is not connected to the supply: a broken wire in its branch, or a missing/loose connection. (A blown L2 would still show 6 V.)
Explain how the voltmeter readings rule out "L2 has blown".
A blown lamp is an open gap, so the voltmeter across it would read the full 6 V. 0 V means no voltage reaches it: the fault is in the wires of its branch.
